q: In a compiler, keywords of a language are recognized during
opts: the lexical analysis of the program
exp:
Compiler ka pehla phase lexical analysis hai jo source ko tokens me todta hai.
Keywords (if, while, int...) bhi tokens hain — scanner inhe identifier se alag pehchanta hai (keyword table / reserved words).
Parser tokens ka use karta hai, unhe recognize nahi karta.
Code generation aur dataflow analysis bahut baad ke phases hain.
Answer: (C)

q: A layer-4 firewall (a device that can look at all protocol headers up to the transport layer) CANNOT
opts: block entire HTTP traffic during 9:00PM and 5:00AM
stop incoming traffic from a specific IP address but allow outgoing traffic to the same IP address
block TCP traffic from a specific user on a multi-user system during 9:00PM and 5:00AM
exp:
Layer-4 firewall IP header (src/dst IP, protocol) aur TCP/UDP header (ports) dekh sakta hai.
(A) HTTP = TCP port 80 → port se block ho jayega (time-based rule possible).
(B) ICMP = IP header ka protocol field → block possible.
(C) Source/destination IP + direction dekh ke possible.
(D) 'Specific user' ki information kisi bhi layer-3/4 header me nahi hoti (same host ke saare users ka IP same) → application/user level info chahiye.
Answer: (D)

q: If two fair coins are flipped and at least one of the outcomes is known to be a head, what is the probability that both outcomes are heads?
exp:
Sample space: {HH, HT, TH, TT}.
Given: at least one head → {HH, HT, TH} (3 equally likely outcomes).
Both heads = {HH} → 1 outcome.
P = 1/3.
Trap: 1/2 mat socho — 'at least one head' ek specific coin ke baare me nahi hai.
Answer: (A)

q:
Consider different activities related to email.
m1: Send an email from a mail client to a mail server
m2: Download an email from mailbox server to a mail client
m3: Checking email in a web browser
Which is the application level protocol used in each activity?
opts: m1: HTTP  m2: SMTP  m3: POP
m1: SMTP  m2: FTP  m3: HTTP
m1: SMTP  m2: POP  m3: HTTP
m1: POP  m2: SMTP  m3: IMAP
exp:
m1: Client se server ko mail bhejna (push) → SMTP.
m2: Mailbox server se client pe mail download karna (pull) → POP (ya IMAP).
m3: Web browser me email (webmail) → HTTP.
So m1: SMTP, m2: POP, m3: HTTP.
Answer: (C)

q:
A company needs to develop a strategy for software product development for which it has a choice of two programming languages L1 and L2. The number of lines of code (LOC) developed using L2 is estimated to be twice the LOC developed with L1. The product will have to be maintained for five years. Various parameters for the company are given in the table below.

Parameter                         | Language L1  | Language L2
Man years needed for development   | LOC/10000    | LOC/10000
Development Cost per man year      | ₹10,00,000   | ₹7,50,000
Maintenance time                   | 5 years      | 5 years
Cost of maintenance per year       | ₹1,00,000    | ₹50,000

Total cost of the project includes cost of development and maintenance. What is the LOC for L1 for which the cost of the project using L1 is equal to the cost of the project using L2?
Let the time taken to switch between user and kernel modes of execution be t₁ while the time taken to switch between two processes be t₂. Which of the following is TRUE?
opts: nothing can be said about the relation between t₁ and t₂
exp:
Mode switch (user ↔ kernel) me sirf CPU mode bit badalta hai aur kuch registers save hote hain.
Process switch me: ek process ka pura context (registers, PC, PCB update) save karna, scheduler chalana, doosre ka context load karna, address space (page table / TLB) change karna padta hai.
Aur process switch ke andar khud mode switch bhi hota hai (kernel me jaana padta hai).
Isliye t₁ < t₂.
Answer: (C)

q: A company needs to develop digital signal processing software for one of its newest inventions. The software is expected to have 40000 lines of code. The company needs to determine the effort in person-months needed to develop this software using the basic COCOMO model. The multiplicative factor for this model is given as 2.8 for the software development on embedded systems, while the exponentiation factor is given as 1.20. What is the estimated effort in person-months?
exp:
Basic COCOMO: Effort = a·(KLOC)^b person-months.
KLOC = 40000/1000 = 40, a = 2.8, b = 1.20.
40^1.2 = e^(1.2·ln40) = e^(1.2·3.689) = e^4.427 ≈ 83.7.
Effort = 2.8 × 83.7 ≈ 234.2 person-months.
Trap: LOC ko KLOC me convert karna zaroori hai (40, not 40000).
Answer: (A)

q: Which of the following pairs have DIFFERENT expressive power?
opts: Deterministic finite automata (DFA) and Non-deterministic finite automata (NFA)
Deterministic push down automata (DPDA) and Non-deterministic push down automata (NPDA)
Deterministic single-tape Turing machine and Non-deterministic single-tape Turing machine
Single-tape Turing machine and multi-tape Turing machine
exp:
DFA ≡ NFA (subset construction) → same power.
DTM ≡ NTM, single-tape TM ≡ multi-tape TM → same power (sirf time differ karta hai).
DPDA sirf deterministic CFLs accept karta hai, NPDA saare CFLs.
Example: {wwᴿ} NPDA se accept hota hai par kisi DPDA se nahi.
Answer: (B)

q: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) has language elements which permit certain actions other than describing the structure of the web document. Which one of the following actions is NOT supported by pure HTML (without any server or client side scripting) pages?
opts: Embed web objects from different sites into the same page
Refresh the page automatically after a specified interval
Automatically redirect to another page upon download
Display the client time as part of the page
exp: (A) ,

q: Which one of the following is NOT desired in a good Software Requirement Specifications (SRS) document?
exp:
SRS batata hai system KYA karega (what), KAISE karega (how) nahi.
Functional + non-functional requirements aur goals of implementation SRS ka part hain.
Algorithms implementation/design detail hain → SRS me nahi hone chahiye.
Answer: (D)

q:
A computer handles several interrupt sources of which the following are relevant for this question.
• Interrupt from CPU temperature sensor (raises interrupt if CPU temperature is too high)
• Interrupt from Mouse (raises interrupt if the mouse is moved or a button is pressed)
• Interrupt from Keyboard (raises interrupt when a key is pressed or released)
• Interrupt from Hard Disk (raises interrupt when a disk read is completed)
Which one of these will be handled at the HIGHEST priority?
exp:
Priority = kitna critical hai / delay se kitna nuksaan.
CPU temperature bahut high → turant action na liya to hardware damage ya system crash.
Mouse/keyboard/disk interrupts thoda delay bardasht kar sakte hain.
Isliye CPU temperature sensor ka interrupt sabse high priority (almost like NMI).
Answer: (D)

q:
Consider a relational table with a single record for each registered student with the following attributes.
1. Registration_Num: Unique registration number of each registered student
2. UID: Unique identity number, unique at the national level for each citizen
3. BankAccount_Num: Unique account number at the bank. A student can have multiple accounts or joint accounts. This attribute stores the primary account number.
4. Name: Name of the student
5. Hostel_Room: Room number of the hostel
Which of the following options is INCORRECT?
opts: Registration_Num can be a primary key
UID is a candidate key if all students are from the same country
If S is a superkey such that S ∩ UID is NULL then S ∪ UID is also a superkey
exp:
(A) Joint accounts possible hain → do students ka primary account same ho sakta hai → BankAccount_Num unique nahi → candidate key NAHI. Yeh statement INCORRECT.
(B) Registration_Num har student ke liye unique → primary key ban sakta hai. Correct.
(C) Sab ek hi country ke → UID unique aur minimal → candidate key. Correct.
(D) Superkey me koi bhi attribute add karo, superkey hi rehta hai. Correct.
Answer: (A)

q:
Which one of the following circuits is NOT equivalent to a 2-input XNOR (exclusive NOR) gate?
(inputs X, Y)
opts: An XOR gate on X and Y, followed by a NOT gate: output = (X ⊕ Y)'
X and Y each pass through a NOT gate, the outputs go to an XOR gate, followed by a NOT gate: output = (X' ⊕ Y')'
X passes through a NOT gate; X' and Y go to an XOR gate (no output inverter): output = X' ⊕ Y

Y is inverted to Y'. AND gate G1 takes X and Y', followed by NOT → (XY')'. OR gate G2 takes Y' and X → (X + Y'). AND gate G3 takes (XY')' and (X + Y'), followed by a NOT gate at the output: output = [(XY')' · (X + Y')]'
exp:
(A) (X⊕Y)' = XNOR. ✓
(B) X'⊕Y' = X⊕Y, uska NOT = XNOR. ✓
(C) X'⊕Y = (X⊕Y)' = XNOR. ✓
(D) (XY')' · (X+Y') = (X'+Y)(X+Y') = X'Y' + XY = XNOR.
Par end me ek aur NOT hai → output = XOR. ✗
Isliye (D) XNOR ke equivalent nahi hai.
Answer: (D)

q:
The simplified SOP (Sum of Product) form of the Boolean expression
(P + Q' + R') · (P + Q' + R) · (P + Q + R')
is
exp:
Har factor ek maxterm hai (PQR order):
(P+Q'+R') = M3 (011), (P+Q'+R) = M2 (010), (P+Q+R') = M1 (001).
F = ΠM(1,2,3) → F = Σm(0,4,5,6,7).
m4..m7 = P (P=1 wale saare), m0 = P'Q'R'.
F = P + P'Q'R' = P + Q'R'.
Answer: (B)

q: The minimum number of D flip-flops needed to design a mod-258 counter is
exp:
n flip-flops se 2ⁿ states milte hain; need 2ⁿ ≥ 258.
2⁸ = 256 < 258, 2⁹ = 512 ≥ 258.
So minimum 9 flip-flops.
Trap: 8 lagana galat — 256 states hi milenge.
Answer: (A)

q: A thread is usually defined as a "light weight process" because an operating system (OS) maintains smaller data structures for a thread than for a process. In relation to this, which of the following is TRUE?
opts: On per-thread basis, the OS maintains only CPU register state
The OS does not maintain a separate stack for each thread
On per-thread basis, the OS does not maintain virtual memory state
On per-thread basis, the OS maintains only scheduling and accounting information
exp:
Threads same process ka address space share karte hain → virtual memory state (page tables) per-process hota hai, per-thread nahi. (C) sahi.
(A) galat: registers ke alawa stack, thread state, scheduling info bhi.
(B) galat: har thread ka alag stack hota hai.
(D) galat: registers/stack bhi maintain hote hain.
Answer: (C)

q:
K4 and Q3 are graphs with the following structures.
K4: complete graph on 4 vertices (drawn as a square with both diagonals).
Q3: 3-dimensional hypercube (cube graph) — 8 vertices, 12 edges, each vertex of degree 3.
Which one of the following statements is TRUE in relation to these graphs?
opts: K4 is planar while Q3 is not
Both K4 and Q3 are planar
Q3 is planar while K3 is not
Neither K4 nor Q3 is planar
exp:
K4: ek diagonal ko square ke bahar se ghuma ke draw karo → koi crossing nahi → planar.
Q3 (cube): inner square andar, outer square bahar, corners jod do → crossing-free drawing → planar.
Check: Q3 me v=8, e=12, bipartite → e ≤ 2v−4 = 12 ✓.
So dono planar.
Answer: (B)

q: If the difference between the expectation of the square of a random variable (E[X²]) and the square of the expectation of the random variable (E[X])² is denoted by R, then
exp:
R = E[X²] − (E[X])² = Var(X) = E[(X − μ)²].
Square ka expectation kabhi negative nahi hota → R ≥ 0.
R = 0 tab jab X constant ho, isliye R > 0 hamesha true nahi.
Answer: (C)

q: The lexical analysis for a modern computer language such as Java needs the power of which one of the following machine models in a necessary and sufficient sense?
exp:
Tokens (identifiers, keywords, numbers, operators) regular expressions se describe hote hain.
Regular languages ke liye finite automata necessary aur sufficient hai.
PDA/TM zyada powerful hain, zaroorat nahi (sufficient but not necessary).
Answer: (A)

q: Let the page fault service time be 10 ms in a computer with average memory access time being 20 ns. If one page fault is generated for every 10⁶ memory accesses, what is the effective access time for the memory?
exp:
Page fault rate p = 1/10⁶.
EAT = (1 − p)·20 ns + p·(10 ms) ≈ 20 ns + 10×10⁶ ns / 10⁶.
= 20 ns + 10 ns = 30 ns (approx, (1−p) ≈ 1).
Answer: (B)

q: Consider a hypothetical processor with an instruction of type LW R1, 20(R2), which during execution reads a 32-bit word from memory and stores it in a 32-bit register R1. The effective address of the memory location is obtained by the addition of a constant 20 and the contents of register R2. Which of the following best reflects the addressing mode implemented by this instruction for the operand in memory?
exp:
EA = 20 + [R2] → register + constant offset (displacement).
Immediate: operand khud instruction me — yahan operand memory me hai. ✗
Register addressing: operand register me. ✗
Scaled: koi scale factor nahi. ✗
Register + offset wala mode options me Base Indexed (base/displacement) addressing se best match karta hai.
Answer: (D)

q: What does the following fragment of C program print?
exp:
c = "GATE2011": p[0]='G', p[1]='A', p[2]='T', p[3]='E'.
p[3] − p[1] = 'E' − 'A' = 69 − 65 = 4.
p + 4 → c[4] se string start → "2011".
printf("%s") wahan se '\0' tak print karega.
Answer: (C)

q:
A max-heap is a heap where the value of each parent is greater than or equal to the value of its children. Which of the following is a max-heap?
(Trees are given in level order; children listed under each parent.)
opts: Root 10; children 8, 6; 8 has left child 4; 6 has children 5 and 2; 5 has left child 1
Root 10; children 8, 6; 8 has children 4, 5; 6 has children 1, 2
Root 10; children 5, 6; 5 has children 4, 8; 6 has children 2, 1
Root 5; children 2, 8; 2 has children 1, 4; 8 has children 6, 10
exp:
Heap = complete binary tree + heap property.
(A) complete nahi: 8 ka right child missing par 5 ka child 1 hai → shape galat.
(B) complete hai; 10≥8,6; 8≥4,5; 6≥1,2 → valid max-heap.
(C) 5 < 8 (child) → property violate.
(D) root 5 < 8, 8 < 10 → violate.
Answer: (B)

q: Let P be a regular language and Q be a context-free language such that Q ⊆ P. (For example, let P be the language represented by the regular expression p*q* and Q be {pⁿqⁿ | n ∈ N}). Then which of the following is ALWAYS regular?
exp:
Regular languages complement ke under closed hain → Σ* − P = P' hamesha regular.
Example se check: P ∩ Q = Q = {pⁿqⁿ} → regular nahi.
P − Q = {pᵐqⁿ | m ≠ n} → regular nahi.
Σ* − Q = complement of {pⁿqⁿ} → regular nahi.
Answer: (C)

q:
An algorithm to find the length of the longest monotonically increasing sequence of numbers in an array A[0 : n−1] is given below.
Let Lᵢ denote the length of the longest monotonically increasing sequence starting at index i in the array.
Initialize Lₙ₋₁ = 1.
For all i such that 0 ≤ i ≤ n−2
  Lᵢ = 1 + Lᵢ₊₁ if A[i] < A[i+1]
  Lᵢ = 1 otherwise
Finally the length of the longest monotonically increasing sequence is Max(L₀, L₁, ..., Lₙ₋₁).
Which of the following statements is TRUE?
opts: The algorithm uses dynamic programming paradigm
The algorithm has a linear complexity and uses branch and bound paradigm
The algorithm has a non-linear polynomial complexity and uses branch and bound paradigm
The algorithm uses divide and conquer paradigm
exp:
Lᵢ ko Lᵢ₊₁ (pehle se computed subproblem) se nikala ja raha hai → recurrence + stored results = dynamic programming.
Right se left ek pass → O(n), linear.
Branch and bound (search tree pruning) ya divide and conquer (problem ko halves me todna) yahan nahi hai.
Answer: (A)

q:
Consider the languages L1, L2 and L3 as given below.
L1 = {0ᵖ1ᵠ | p, q ∈ N},
L2 = {0ᵖ1ᵠ | p, q ∈ N and p = q} and
L3 = {0ᵖ1ᵠ0ʳ | p, q, r ∈ N and p = q = r}.
Which of the following statements is NOT TRUE?
opts: Push Down Automata (PDA) can be used to recognize L1 and L2
All the three languages are context free
Turing machines can be used to recognize all the languages
exp:
L1 = 0*1* → regular (isliye CFL bhi). (B) true.
L2 = {0ⁿ1ⁿ} → CFL, PDA se recognize hota hai. L1 bhi PDA se. (A) true.
L3 = {0ⁿ1ⁿ0ⁿ} → teen counts compare karne hain, ek stack se nahi hoga → CFL nahi (pumping lemma for CFL). Yeh context-sensitive hai.
Isliye 'All three are context free' NOT TRUE.
TM teeno ko recognize kar sakta hai. (D) true.
Answer: (C)

q:
Consider two binary operators '↑' and '↓' with the precedence of operator ↓ being lower than that of the operator ↑. Operator ↑ is right associative while operator ↓ is left associative. Which one of the following represents the parse tree for expression (7↓3↑4↑3↓2)?
(Each option's parse tree is written in fully parenthesized form; the outermost operator is the root.)
exp:
↑ ki precedence zyada → pehle 3↑4↑3 group hoga.
↑ right associative → 3↑(4↑3).
Ab expression: 7 ↓ [3↑(4↑3)] ↓ 2.
↓ left associative → (7 ↓ [3↑(4↑3)]) ↓ 2.
Root = second ↓, left child = first ↓ (7 aur ↑-subtree), right child = 2.
Yeh option (B) ka tree hai.
Answer: (B)

q:
On a non-pipelined sequential processor, a program segment, which is a part of the interrupt service routine, is given to transfer 500 bytes from an I/O device to memory.

Assume that each statement in this program is equivalent to a machine instruction which takes one clock cycle to execute if it is a non-load/store instruction. The load-store instructions take two clock cycles to execute.
The designer of the system also has an alternate approach of using the DMA controller to implement the same transfer. The DMA controller requires 20 clock cycles for initialization and other overheads. Each DMA transfer cycle takes two clock cycles to transfer one byte of data from the device to the memory.
What is the approximate speedup when the DMA controller based design is used in place of the interrupt driven program based input-output?
code:
Initialize the address register
        Initialize the count to 500
LOOP:   Load a byte from device
        Store in memory at address given by address register
        Increment the address register
        Decrement the count
        If count != 0 go to LOOP
exp:
Program based: 2 init instructions = 2 cycles.
Loop per byte: Load (2) + Store (2) + Increment (1) + Decrement (1) + Branch (1) = 7 cycles.
Total = 2 + 500×7 = 3502 cycles.
DMA: 20 + 500×2 = 1020 cycles.
Speedup = 3502/1020 ≈ 3.43.
Answer: (A)

q: We are given a set of n distinct elements and an unlabeled binary tree with n nodes. In how many ways can we populate the tree with the given set so that it becomes a binary search tree?
exp:
BST ka inorder traversal hamesha sorted order deta hai.
Tree ka shape fixed hai → uska inorder sequence of nodes fixed hai.
Sorted elements ko usi inorder order me nodes me bharna padega → sirf ek hi tareeka.
Trap: (1/(n+1))·²ⁿCₙ = number of different BST shapes hai, yahan shape pehle se diya hai.
Answer: (B)

q:
Which one of the following options is CORRECT given three positive integers x, y and z, and a predicate
P(x) = ¬(x = 1) ∧ ∀y (∃z (x = y * z) ⇒ (y = x) ∨ (y = 1))
opts: P(x) being true means that x is a prime number
P(x) being true means that x is a number other than 1
P(x) is always true irrespective of the value of x
P(x) being true means that x has exactly two factors other than 1 and x
exp:
¬(x = 1): x, 1 nahi hai.
∃z (x = y*z): y, x ka divisor hai.
∀y (y divides x ⇒ y = x ya y = 1): x ke sirf do divisors — 1 aur x khud.
x ≠ 1 aur sirf divisors 1, x → x prime hai.
Answer: (A)

q:
Given i = √(−1), what will be the evaluation of the definite integral
∫₀^(π/2) (cos x + i sin x)/(cos x − i sin x) dx ?
exp:
cos x + i sin x = e^(ix), cos x − i sin x = e^(−ix).
Integrand = e^(ix)/e^(−ix) = e^(2ix).
∫₀^(π/2) e^(2ix) dx = [e^(2ix)/(2i)]₀^(π/2) = (e^(iπ) − 1)/(2i).
e^(iπ) = −1 → (−2)/(2i) = −1/i = i (kyunki 1/i = −i).
Answer: (D)

q:
Consider a database table T containing two columns X and Y each of type integer. After the creation of the table, one record (X=1, Y=1) is inserted in the table.
Let MX and MY denote the respective maximum values of X and Y among all records in the table at any point in time. Using MX and MY, new records are inserted in the table 128 times with X and Y values being MX+1, 2*MY+1 respectively. It may be noted that each time after the insertion, values of MX and MY change.
What will be the output of the following SQL query after the steps mentioned above are carried out?
code: SELECT Y FROM T WHERE X=7;
exp:
Start: (1, 1).
Har insert: X = MX+1, Y = 2·MY+1.
(2, 3), (3, 7), (4, 15), (5, 31), (6, 63), (7, 127), ...
Pattern: Y = 2^X − 1 → X = 7 pe Y = 2⁷ − 1 = 127.
128 inserts sirf itna ensure karte hain ki X=7 wala row exist karta hai.
Answer: (A)

q: Consider a finite sequence of random values X = [x₁, x₂, ..., xₙ]. Let μₓ be the mean and σₓ be the standard deviation of X. Let another finite sequence Y of equal length be derived from this as yᵢ = a * xᵢ + b, where a and b are positive constants. Let μᵧ be the mean and σᵧ be the standard deviation of this sequence. Which one of the following statements is INCORRECT?
opts: Index position of mode of X in X is the same as the index position of mode of Y in Y.
Index position of median of X in X is the same as the index position of median of Y in Y.
exp:
y = ax + b with a > 0 → increasing one-to-one map, order preserve hota hai.
Isliye mode aur median same index pe milenge. (A), (B) correct.
Mean linear hai: μᵧ = aμₓ + b. (C) correct.
SD pe shift (b) ka koi effect nahi: σᵧ = |a|·σₓ = aσₓ, not aσₓ + b.
So (D) INCORRECT.
Answer: (D)

q: A deck of 5 cards (each carrying a distinct number from 1 to 5) is shuffled thoroughly. Two cards are then removed one at a time from the deck. What is the probability that the two cards are selected with the number on the first card being one higher than the number on the second card?
exp:
Ordered pairs (first, second) without replacement: 5 × 4 = 20.
Favourable: first = second + 1 → (2,1), (3,2), (4,3), (5,4) = 4.
P = 4/20 = 1/5.
Trap: 4/25 tab aata jab replacement hota.
Answer: (A)

q:
Consider the following table of arrival time and burst time for three processes P0, P1 and P2.
Process | Arrival time | Burst Time
P0      | 0 ms         | 9 ms
P1      | 1 ms         | 4 ms
P2      | 2 ms         | 9 ms
The pre-emptive shortest job first scheduling algorithm is used. Scheduling is carried out only at arrival or completion of processes. What is the average waiting time for the three processes?
exp:
t=0: P0 start. t=1: P1 aaya (4) < P0 remaining (8) → preempt, P1 run.
t=2: P2 aaya (9), P1 remaining 3 → P1 continue, t=5 pe complete.
t=5: P0 rem 8 vs P2 9 → P0 run 5–13. Phir P2 13–22.
Waiting = completion − arrival − burst:
P0 = 13−0−9 = 4, P1 = 5−1−4 = 0, P2 = 22−2−9 = 11.
Avg = 15/3 = 5.0 ms.
Answer: (A)

q:
Consider evaluating the following expression tree on a machine with load-store architecture in which memory can be accessed only through load and store instructions. The variables a, b, c, d and e are initially stored in memory. The binary operators used in this expression tree can be evaluated by the machine only when the operands are in registers. The instructions produce result only in a register. If no intermediate results can be stored in memory, what is the minimum number of registers needed to evaluate this expression?
Expression tree: root '+' with left child '−'(a, b) and right child '−'(e, '+'(c, d)), i.e. (a − b) + (e − (c + d)).
exp:
Deeper (right) subtree pehle evaluate karo:
R1 ← c, R2 ← d, R1 ← R1 + R2 (c+d)
R2 ← e, R2 ← R2 − R1 (e−(c+d)) → result R2 me hold.
Ab left: R1 ← a, R3 ← b, R1 ← R1 − R3 (a−b).
R1 ← R1 + R2.
Left subtree ko 2 registers chahiye aur tab tak right ka result ek register me hold hai → 3.
Answer: (D)

q:
Which of the given options provides the increasing order of asymptotic complexity of functions f₁, f₂, f₃ and f₄?
f₁(n) = 2ⁿ   f₂(n) = n^(3/2)   f₃(n) = n log₂ n   f₄(n) = n^(log₂ n)
exp:
Log le ke compare karo (log₂):
f₃: log n + log log n, f₂: 1.5 log n, f₄: (log n)², f₁: n.
log n + log log n < 1.5 log n < (log n)² < n (large n).
So f₃ < f₂ < f₄ < f₁.
Trap: n^(log n) quasi-polynomial hai — har polynomial se bada par 2ⁿ se chhota.
Answer: (A)

q:
Four matrices M₁, M₂, M₃ and M₄ of dimensions p×q, q×r, r×s and s×t respectively can be multiplied in several ways with different number of total scalar multiplications. For example when multiplied as ((M₁×M₂)×(M₃×M₄)), the total number of scalar multiplications is pqr + rst + prt. When multiplied as (((M₁×M₂)×M₃)×M₄), the total number of scalar multiplications is pqr + prs + pst.
If p = 10, q = 100, r = 20, s = 5, and t = 80, then the minimum number of scalar multiplications needed is

Consider a relational table r with sufficient number of records, having attributes A₁, A₂, ..., Aₙ and let 1 ≤ p ≤ n. Two queries Q1 and Q2 are given below.
Q1: π_{A₁,...,Aₚ}(σ_{Aₚ = c}(r)) where c is a constant
Q2: π_{A₁,...,Aₚ}(σ_{c₁ ≤ Aₚ ≤ c₂}(r)) where c₁ and c₂ are constants
The database can be configured to do ordered indexing on Aₚ or hashing on Aₚ. Which of the following statements is TRUE?
opts: Ordered indexing will always outperform hashing for both queries
Hashing will always outperform ordered indexing for both queries
Hashing will outperform ordered indexing on Q1, but not on Q2
Hashing will outperform ordered indexing on Q2, but not on Q1
exp:
Q1 equality search hai (Aₚ = c): hashing se ~O(1) me bucket mil jata hai → hashing better.
Q2 range query hai (c₁ ≤ Aₚ ≤ c₂): hashing order preserve nahi karta, range ke liye useless.
Ordered index (B+ tree) me c₁ dhundo, phir leaf pe sequentially aage badho → better.
Answer: (C)

[[1, 2, 3], [0, 4, 7], [0, 0, 3]]
Which one of the following options provides the CORRECT values of the eigenvalues of the matrix?
exp:
Matrix upper triangular hai.

det(A − λI) = (1−λ)(4−λ)(3−λ) = 0 → λ = 1, 4, 3.

q:
Consider an instruction pipeline with four stages (S1, S2, S3 and S4) each with combinational circuit only. The pipeline registers are required between each stage and at the end of the last stage. Delays for the stages and for the pipeline registers are as given in the figure:
S1 (5 ns) → Pipeline Register (1 ns) → S2 (6 ns) → Pipeline Register (1 ns) → S3 (11 ns) → Pipeline Register (1 ns) → S4 (8 ns) → Pipeline Register (1 ns)
What is the approximate speed up of the pipeline in steady state under ideal conditions when compared to the corresponding non-pipeline implementation?
exp:
Non-pipelined: sirf combinational delays, registers nahi → 5 + 6 + 11 + 8 = 30 ns per instruction.
Pipelined clock = max stage delay + register delay = 11 + 1 = 12 ns.
Steady state me har 12 ns me ek instruction complete.
Speedup = 30/12 = 2.5.
Trap: non-pipelined me register delay add mat karo.
Answer: (B)

Mod n counter chahiye: n states (remainder 0..n−1).

q:
An 8KB direct-mapped write-back cache is organized as multiple blocks, each of size 32-bytes. The processor generates 32-bit addresses. The cache controller maintains the tag information for each cache block comprising of the following.
1 Valid bit
1 Modified bit
As many bits as the minimum needed to identify the memory block mapped in the cache.
What is the total size of memory needed at the cache controller to store meta-data (tags) for the cache?
exp:
Lines = 8KB/32B = 2¹³/2⁵ = 2⁸ = 256.
Offset = 5 bits, index = 8 bits, tag = 32 − 5 − 8 = 19 bits.
Per line metadata = 19 + 1 (valid) + 1 (modified) = 21 bits.
Total = 256 × 21 = 5376 bits.
Answer: (D)

q: An application loads 100 libraries at startup. Loading each library requires exactly one disk access. The seek time of the disk to a random location is given as 10 ms. Rotational speed of disk is 6000 rpm. If all 100 libraries are loaded from random locations on the disk, how long does it take to load all libraries? (The time to transfer data from the disk block once the head has been positioned at the start of the block may be neglected.)
exp:
6000 rpm → 100 rotations/s → 1 rotation = 10 ms.
Avg rotational latency = half rotation = 5 ms.
Ek access = seek + latency = 10 + 5 = 15 ms (transfer neglect).
100 libraries = 100 × 15 ms = 1500 ms = 1.5 s.
Trap: rotational latency average half rotation hota hai, full nahi.
Answer: (B)

q:
A deterministic finite automaton (DFA) D with alphabet Σ = {a, b} is given below.
States: p (start), q, r, s (final), t (final).
Transitions: p –a→ s, p –b→ q, q –a→ t, q –b→ r, r –a,b→ r, s –a,b→ s, t –a,b→ t.
Which of the following finite state machines is a valid minimal DFA which accepts the same language as D?
opts: States p (start), q, r, s (final). p –a→ s, p –b→ q, q –a→ s, q –b→ r, r –a,b→ r, s –a,b→ s
States p (start), q (final), r (final), s. p –a,b→ q, q –b→ s, q –a→ r, s –a,b→ s, r –a,b→ r
States p (start), q (final), r. p –a,b→ q, q –a,b→ q, q –b→ r, r –a,b→ r
States p (start), q, s (final). p –a→ s, p –b→ q, q –b→ q, q –a→ s, s –a,b→ s
exp:
D ki language: string 'a' se shuru ho (p→s) ya 'ba' se shuru ho (p→q→t); 'bb' se shuru → dead state r.
s aur t dono final hain aur dono pe a,b ka self-loop hai → equivalent, merge karo.
Minimal DFA: p, q, r (dead), s (final) — 4 states. Yeh bilkul (A) hai.
(B) 'b' ya 'a' single string accept karta hai (q final) — galat language.
(C) q pe b ke do transitions → DFA hi nahi.
(D) q –b→ q loop → 'bba' accept karega, jo D reject karta hai.
Answer: (A)

q:
The following is the comment written for a C function.

A software test engineer is assigned the job of doing black box testing. He comes up with the following test cases, many of which are redundant.
Test Case | a   | b     | c    | root1 | root2 | Return Value
T1        | 0.0 | 0.0   | 7.0  | 0.0   | 0.0   | −1
T2        | 0.0 | 1.0   | 3.0  | 0.0   | 0.0   | −1
T3        | 1.0 | 2.0   | 1.0  | −1.0  | −1.0  | 0
T4        | 4.0 | −12.0 | 9.0  | 1.5   | 1.5   | 0
T5        | 1.0 | −2.0  | −3.0 | 3.0   | −1.0  | 0
T6        | 1.0 | 1.0   | 4.0  | 0.0   | 0.0   | −1
Which one of the following options provide the set of non-redundant tests using equivalence class partitioning approach from input perspective for black box testing?
code:
/* This function computes the roots of a quadratic equation
   a.x^2 + b.x + c = 0. The function stores two real roots
   in *root1 and *root2 and returns the status of validity
   of roots. It handles four different kinds of cases.
   (i) When coefficient a is zero irrespective of discriminant
   (ii) When discriminant is positive
   (iii) When discriminant is zero
   (iv) When discriminant is negative.
   Only in case (ii) and (iii), the stored roots are valid.
   Otherwise 0 is stored in the roots. The function returns
   0 when the roots are valid and -1 otherwise.
   The function also ensures root1 >= root2.
      int get_QuadRoots(float a, float b, float c,
          float *root1, float *root2);
*/
exp:
Input ke 4 equivalence classes: (i) a = 0, (ii) D > 0, (iii) D = 0, (iv) D < 0.
T1, T2: a = 0 → class (i) (ek hi chahiye).
T3: D = 4 − 4 = 0 → (iii). T4: D = 144 − 144 = 0 → (iii).
T5: D = 4 + 12 = 16 > 0 → (ii). T6: D = 1 − 16 < 0 → (iv).
Non-redundant set me har class se ek test: {T1/T2, T3/T4, T5, T6}.
Options me sirf (C) T2, T4, T5, T6 charon classes cover karta hai.
Answer: (C)

q:
Common Data for Questions 50 and 51: Consider the following circuit involving three D-type flip-flops used in a certain type of counter configuration.
Circuit (from the figure): three D flip-flops with outputs P, Q and R, all on the same clock.
D input of P flip-flop = R
D input of Q flip-flop = NOR(P, R) = (P + R)'
D input of R flip-flop = AND(Q, R') where R' is the Q̄ output of the R flip-flop

If at some instance prior to the occurrence of the clock edge, P, Q and R have a value 0, 1 and 0 respectively, what shall be the value of PQR after the clock edge?
exp:
Next-state equations: P⁺ = R, Q⁺ = (P + R)', R⁺ = Q·R'.
Present PQR = 010.
P⁺ = R = 0.
Q⁺ = (0 + 0)' = 1.
R⁺ = Q·R' = 1·1 = 1.
Next PQR = 011.
Answer: (D)

Statement for Linked Answer Questions 52 and 53: Consider a network with five nodes, N1 to N5, as shown below.
Links (cost): N1–N2 (1), N2–N5 (3), N2–N3 (6), N5–N4 (4), N4–N3 (2).
The network uses a Distance Vector Routing protocol. Once the routes have stabilized, the distance vectors at different nodes are as following.
N1: (0, 1, 7, 8, 4)
N2: (1, 0, 6, 7, 3)
N3: (7, 6, 0, 2, 6)
N4: (8, 7, 2, 0, 4)
N5: (4, 3, 6, 4, 0)
Each distance vector is the distance of the best known path at that instance to nodes, N1 to N5, where the distance to itself is 0. Also, all links are symmetric and the cost is identical in both directions. In each round, all nodes exchange their distance vectors with their respective neighbors. Then all nodes update their distance vectors. In between two rounds, any change in cost of a link will cause the two incident nodes to change only that entry in their distance vectors.

The cost of link N2-N3 reduces to 2 (in both directions). After the next round of updates, what will be the new distance vector at node, N3?
exp:
Link change ke baad: N2 ka vector (1, 0, 2, 7, 3), N3 ka N2 entry = 2.
N3 ke neighbours: N2 (cost 2), N4 (cost 2); N4 = (8, 7, 2, 0, 4).
To N1: min(2 + 1, 2 + 8) = 3.
To N2: min(2 + 0, 2 + 7) = 2.
To N4: min(2 + 7, 2 + 0) = 2.
To N5: min(2 + 3, 2 + 4) = 5.
N3 = (3, 2, 0, 2, 5).
Answer: (A)

q:
Statement for Linked Answer Questions 52 and 53: Consider a network with five nodes, N1 to N5, as shown below.
Links (cost): N1–N2 (1), N2–N5 (3), N2–N3 (6), N5–N4 (4), N4–N3 (2).
The network uses a Distance Vector Routing protocol. Once the routes have stabilized, the distance vectors at different nodes are as following.
N1: (0, 1, 7, 8, 4)
N2: (1, 0, 6, 7, 3)
N3: (7, 6, 0, 2, 6)
N4: (8, 7, 2, 0, 4)
N5: (4, 3, 6, 4, 0)
Each distance vector is the distance of the best known path at that instance to nodes, N1 to N5, where the distance to itself is 0. Also, all links are symmetric and the cost is identical in both directions. In each round, all nodes exchange their distance vectors with their respective neighbors. Then all nodes update their distance vectors. In between two rounds, any change in cost of a link will cause the two incident nodes to change only that entry in their distance vectors.

The cost of link N2-N3 reduces to 2 (in both directions). After the next round of updates, the new distance vector at node N3 is computed.
After the update in the previous question, the link N1-N2 goes down. N2 will reflect this change immediately in its distance vector as cost, ∞. After the NEXT ROUND of update, what will be the cost to N1 in the distance vector of N3?
exp:
Pichle round ke baad N4 ne bhi update kiya tha (N3 ka purana vector (7,6,0,2,6) aur N5 ka (4,…) use karke): N4 → N1 = min(2 + 7, 4 + 4) = 8.
Ab N1–N2 link down → N2 ka N1 entry = ∞.
Next round me N3 ko milta hai: N2 se ∞, N4 se 8.
N3 → N1 = min(2 + ∞, 2 + 8) = 10.
Trap: N3 ka apna purana 3 use nahi hota — naya value neighbours ke vectors se hi banta hai (count-to-infinity ki shuruaat).
Answer: (C)

q:
Statement for Linked Answer Questions 54 and 55: An undirected graph G(V, E) contains n (n > 2) nodes named v₁, v₂, ..., vₙ. Two nodes vᵢ, vⱼ are connected if and only if 0 < |i − j| ≤ 2. Each edge (vᵢ, vⱼ) is assigned a weight i + j. A sample graph with n = 4 has edges v1–v2 (3), v1–v3 (4), v2–v3 (5), v2–v4 (6), v3–v4 (7).

What will be the cost of the minimum spanning tree (MST) of such a graph with n nodes?
exp:
Edges: (vᵢ, vᵢ₊₁) weight 2i+1, (vᵢ, vᵢ₊₂) weight 2i+2.
Kruskal: 3 (v1v2), 4 (v1v3) lo; 5 (v2v3) cycle banata hai → skip; 6 (v2v4) lo; 7 (v3v4) cycle → skip; 8 (v3v5) lo ...
Pattern: MST = (v1,v2) + saare (vᵢ, vᵢ₊₂) edges, i = 1..n−2.
Cost = 3 + Σᵢ₌₁ⁿ⁻² (2i + 2) = 3 + (n−2)(n−1) + 2(n−2) = 3 + (n−2)(n+1) = n² − n + 1.
Check n = 4: 3 + 4 + 6 = 13 = 16 − 4 + 1 ✓.
Answer: (B)

q:
Statement for Linked Answer Questions 54 and 55: An undirected graph G(V, E) contains n (n > 2) nodes named v₁, v₂, ..., vₙ. Two nodes vᵢ, vⱼ are connected if and only if 0 < |i − j| ≤ 2. Each edge (vᵢ, vⱼ) is assigned a weight i + j. A sample graph with n = 4 has edges v1–v2 (3), v1–v3 (4), v2–v3 (5), v2–v4 (6), v3–v4 (7).

q:
P, Q, R and S are four types of dangerous microbes recently found in a human habitat. The area of each circle with its diameter printed in brackets represents the growth of a single microbe surviving human immunity system within 24 hours of entering the body. The danger to human beings varies proportionately with the toxicity, potency and growth attributed to a microbe shown in the figure below:
Bubble chart — x-axis: Potency (probability that microbe will overcome human immunity system), 0.2 to 1; y-axis: Toxicity (milligrams of microbe required to destroy half of the body mass in kilograms), 0 to 1000.
P (50 mm): potency 0.4, toxicity 800
Q (40 mm): potency 0.5, toxicity 600
R (30 mm): potency 0.4, toxicity 300
S (20 mm): potency 0.8, toxicity 200
A pharmaceutical company is contemplating the development of a vaccine against the most dangerous microbe. Which microbe should the company target in its first attempt?
exp:
Toxicity axis = kitne mg chahiye destroy karne ke liye → value jitni KAM, microbe utna zyada toxic. So effective toxicity ∝ 1/y.
Growth ∝ area ∝ d².
Danger ∝ potency × d² / y:
P: 0.4 × 2500 / 800 = 1.25
Q: 0.5 × 1600 / 600 ≈ 1.33
R: 0.4 × 900 / 300 = 1.2
S: 0.8 × 400 / 200 = 1.6 → maximum.
Trap: y-value ko seedha toxicity maan lena (bada = zyada toxic) galat hai.
Answer: (D)

q: The variable cost (V) of manufacturing a product varies according to the equation V = 4q, where q is the quantity produced. The fixed cost (F) of production of same product reduces with q according to the equation F = 100/q. How many units should be produced to minimize the total cost (V+F)?

A transporter receives the same number of orders each day. Currently, he has some pending orders (backlog) to be shipped. If he uses 7 trucks, then at the end of the 4th day he can clear all the orders. Alternatively, if he uses only 3 trucks, then all the orders are cleared at the end of the 10th day. What is the minimum number of trucks required so that there will be no pending order at the end of the 5th day?
exp:
Backlog = B, daily orders = x, ek truck per day = c capacity.
7 trucks, 4 days: 28c = B + 4x. 3 trucks, 10 days: 30c = B + 10x.
Subtract: 2c = 6x → x = c/3; B = 28c − 4c/3 = 80c/3.
5 days: n·5c ≥ B + 5x = 80c/3 + 5c/3 = 85c/3 → n ≥ 17/3 ≈ 5.67.
Minimum integer n = 6.
Answer: (C)

q: A container originally contains 10 litres of pure spirit. From this container 1 litre of spirit is replaced with 1 litre of water. Subsequently, 1 litre of the mixture is again replaced with 1 litre of water and this process is repeated one more time. How much spirit is now left in the container?
exp:
Har replacement pe spirit (1 − 1/10) = 0.9 guna reh jata hai.
Total 3 replacements (ek, phir ek aur, phir 'one more time').
Spirit = 10 × (0.9)³ = 10 × 0.729 = 7.29 litres.
Trap: simple 10 − 3 = 7 galat hai — baad me nikla mixture pure spirit nahi hai.
Answer: (D)
